subject: Follow-up: NovaHealth pilot — KMS & encryption requirements
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Judy Park <judy.park@novahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:08:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: NovaHealth pilot — KMS & encryption requirements

Hi Judy — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can scope the pilot: 

1) Summary of what we heard (please correct me if I missed anything):
- Pilot scope: embed Redwood inference for clinical notes summarization in a non-prod environment, then evaluate production cutover timeline.
- Data classification: PHI will be in-scope for production; non-prod dataset will be masked but must follow same encryption-in-transit expectations.
- Compliance drivers: HIPAA + SOC 2 Type II controls required for vendor selection; also need GDPR DPA for EU data.

2) Specific asks you raised around encryption/KMS:
- Do you require customer-managed keys (CMK) / BYOK for production?
- If CMK is required, does NovaHealth require HSM-backed keys (e.g., AWS CloudHSM, Azure HSM) or will a KMS with CMEK be acceptable?
- Do you need key rotation policies or import/export restrictions documented?

3) Our immediate offers / what we can provide this week:
- Short answers on our SOC 2 status and timeline for evidence access.
- A one-page KMS configuration summary showing supported key providers, HSM options, and sample architecture for private deployments.
- The vendor security questionnaire (if you can share the NovaHealth template) — we can pre-fill the crypto/encryption sections for speed.

Next steps I propose:
- Judy: share the NovaHealth vendor questionnaire (or a link) and clarify whether CMK + HSM are mandatory for production.
- Monica: I will attach the Redwood KMS summary and a short SOC 2 evidence checklist (well send by EOD).
- Lauren: to coordinate a technical follow-up call (30 minutes) next week to run through architecture options.

Thanks — Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_KMS_Configuration_Summary.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)
From: Judy Park <judy.park@novahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaHealth Security <security@novahealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T20:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: NovaHealth pilot — KMS & encryption requirements

Rafael — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers up front: 

- CMK/BYOK: For production PHI, NovaHealth requires customer-managed keys that are HSM-backed. We use AWS CloudHSM for most vendors, but we can evaluate alternatives if you provide equivalent attestations.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ is standard; we will expect mutual TLS for any private deployment endpoints.
- Key rotation & policy: We require a documented rotation policy and the ability to rotate keys without data loss during a maintenance window.

I attached our vendor security questionnaire (VQ-vNovaHealth-2026.docx) and highlighted the crypto and key-management sections we need completed first. Were also happy to accept a redline if any items are not applicable.

Proposed timeline: if Redwood can return the completed crypto sections by 2026-11-18, our security team will do a first pass and get back with clarifying items by 2026-11-22.

-Judy

--
Judy Park
Lead Information Security Analyst | NovaHealth
judy.park@novahealth.com

Attachments: NovaHealth_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_v1.2.docx (DOCX, 350KB)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Judy Park <judy.park@novahealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: NovaHealth pilot — KMS & encryption requirements

Thanks Judy — attaching the filled KMS summary and a short SOC 2 evidence table. A couple of clarifications from our tech team as we fill the questionnaire: 

- Deployment modes: we support (1) Hosted API with Redwood-managed keys, (2) Dedicated reserved capacity with tenant isolation, and (3) Private (VPC/on-prem) where customers can bring their own keys to an HSM. For NovaHealth production PHI use-case we recommend the Private deployment with CMK in your HSM.
- HSM integration: our Private offering supports external HSMs via a KMIP-compatible gateway; for AWS CloudHSM we can integrate via a VPC peering and customer-managed CloudHSM cluster.
- Key access & logging: key usage is logged and can be shipped to your SIEM; we can provide sample CloudTrail/KMS logs or an audit bundle as part of SOC 2 evidence.

Questions for you to confirm in the questionnaire: 
- Will NovaHealth provide the CloudHSM cluster, or do you expect Redwood to provision and attach?
- Do you have a preferred KMS provider (AWS KMS vs. Azure Key Vault vs. GCP KMS) for this pilot?

We aim to return the highlighted crypto sections and SOC 2 evidence checklist by EOD 2026-11-18. If that timeline works, can we lock an architectural sync for 2026-11-19 at 10:00am PT? Lauren — can you set the invite and include our infra lead?

Thanks,
Monica 

--
Monica Patel
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Monica / Rafael — that timeline looks good. A few final notes before the sync: 

- NovaHealth will provide and manage the CloudHSM cluster for vendors that require HSM-backed CMKs. We will share connectivity details (VPC, peering, and IAM principals) once the MOU is in place.
- Ive attached the official PDF of our vendor questionnaire (final) — please return the completed crypto and logging sections by end of day 2026-11-18 as discussed.
- Security sync confirmed: 2026-11-19 10:00am PT. Please include any network diagrams in the invite.

Thanks — looking forward to the prep materials.

-Judy
